column1: # GitHub identities on this machine — the single source of truth. Both the skill
# (guidance) and gh-identity-guard.sh (enforcement) resolve through this file;
# do not restate the mapping anywhere else.
#   ssh-host        the Host alias in ~/.ssh/config used by the repository's
#                   remote — the strong signal, matched first
#   owner           the GitHub org/user that owns the repository; the fallback
#                   when a remote uses plain github.com
#   expected-login  what `gh <alias> api user --jq .login` must return
# Define each alias in ~/.config/gh/config.yml so it resolves that account's own
# token instead of the globally active one:
#     personal: '!GH_TOKEN="$(gh auth token --hostname github.com --user octocat)" gh "$@"'
# Every row below is commented out, so nothing resolves yet and the hook blocks
# every `gh` command that could act on a repository. That is deliberate: an
# unconfigured guard must not fall back to the active account. Uncomment and edit.
